newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Police find remains of cult member in Ethiopia.
newsitem.headline: Police find remains of cult member in Ethiopia.

text.p: Ethiopian police said on Wednesday they had found the charred remains of a woman suspected of being a member of a cult that believed in living without food.
A police statement said remains of the woman, who had survived for 50 days without food, were found in a house in Nazaret town, 100 km (60 miles) east of the capital Addis Ababa.
Police said a 36-year-old university dropout had converted his family of eight to believe people could survive on the holy spirit and without food, and the group only chewed qat and drank water.
Qat is the leaf of a mildly narcotic plant widely chewed in East Africa.

Police said they suspected the dead woman was the sister of the cult leader, whose mother had also died. They said they believed the sister died from starvation and her body was burned to stop it rotting.
Police said the cult leader, whose name was withheld, and another sister were being held in custody and a search was on for other members of the cult.
